rules.when: The task is a trivial change whose edit is already fully defined, such as a one-line fix, a config value change, or a rote rename.
rules.why: Trivial fixers: the change is already specified, so the cheapest fast model is enough.

rules.when: The task is planning a new feature, writing a spec, or investigating a complex or not yet understood bug.
rules.why: Planners: Opus 5.5 leads because only the frontier tier asks what the real goal is instead of how to get it done (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104749177456722354). GPT 6 Sol stays as the quota-driven stand-in: it is now roughly a Sonnet-equivalent implementer tier (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104657437777408400), so it takes planning when Claude's window is exhausted rather than as an equal planner. xhigh because the work is not well defined yet.

rules.when: The task is an adversarial code review or audit of an existing change.
rules.why: GPT 6 Sol is the strongest adversarial reviewer at volume; Opus 5.5 takes the review when Codex quota is unavailable.

rules.when: The task is highly ambiguous or creative work that truly needs premium intelligence, or an escalation to untangle a mess such as crewmates disagreeing, a spiraling review loop, or a simple change that grew into a giant PR.
rules.why: Premium intelligence is expensive; use it only when the extra judgment is worth the cost. Opus 5.5 stands in when Fable quota is tight.

why: Implementers: well-defined work goes to the fast, capable implementer tier rather than the frontier planner. Claude Sonnet 5.5 leads (faster, cheaper, and smart enough to follow a plan) and GPT 6 Sol is its equal in this tier, so live quota picks whichever account has room (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104749177456722354, x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104657437777408400).
